newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-MIXED FEELINGS FOR RETIRING CAMPESE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MIXED FEELINGS FOR RETIRING CAMPESE.

text.p: David Campese admitted to mixed emotions as he departed test rugby after Australia's 28-19 win over Wales on Sunday.

Campese, the world's record try-scorer whose tally has finally stopped at 64 after 101 internationals, was delighted to finish on the winning side in his last test but confessed he would miss wearing the Wallaby jersey.
"To win today was fantastic, to go out on such a great note. But my life has been with the Wallabies so the next time I see the guys playing will be disheartening for me.

"I'll miss listening to the coach telling me why I'm dropped, but the thing I'll miss most is being around guys like Tim Horan and Jason Little and being associated with so many fantastic young players."
Campese was given a rousing ovation by the Welsh crowd at the end, but could not totally avoid controversy on an otherwise quiet afternoon.

He appeared to knock the ball on in midfield in the move which led to Australia's first try, and grinned broadly when the subject was mentioned afterwards. "I'm not going to say I did or I didn't," he said. "The ref gave the try and that's that."
The 34-year-old winger still hopes to play against the Barbarians in the end-of-tour game at Twickenham next Saturday, and Wallaby skipper Horan was quick to pay tribute to his team mate.

"We'll miss the friendship he gives to other players and his experience. Even today, with 10 minutes to go, he called everyone in and calmed them down. He's left behind a great spirit that hopefully the younger guys can carry on."
